description: The chart illustrates the number of hateful communication datasets released per year, broken down by language categories. The horizontal axis contains the categories “Year,” labeled with years from 2012 through 2021 in chronological order. The vertical axis is labeled “Number of datasets” and uses a logarithmic scale with major ticks at approximately \(10^0\), \(10^1\), and \(10^2\) (covering roughly 1 to 100 datasets). Bars are color-coded by the legend titled “Language”: English (blue), All other (orange), Arabic (green), Bengali (red), Spanish (purple), and Russian (brown). For 2012–2015, only English bars appear, each at a low single-digit level (around 2–3). In 2016, English is around 10 and “All other” is around 3. In 2017, English is in the low tens (around the mid‑20s), “All other” is in the mid‑teens, Arabic is around 3, Bengali is around 1, and Spanish is around 4. In 2018, English is around the low‑30s, “All other” is around the low‑teens, Arabic is around 5, and Bengali is around 1. In 2019, English is around 40, “All other” is around the low‑20s, Arabic is around 4, Bengali is around 2, Spanish is around 4, and Russian is around 6. In 2020, English is near the upper end of the axis (around 80–90), “All other” is also near that level (around 80), Arabic is around 7, Bengali is around 4, Spanish is around 10, and Russian is around 9. In 2021, English is near the top of the scale (around 90), “All other” is around 40, Bengali is around 13, Spanish is around 11, and Russian is around 9 (no Arabic bar is visible for 2021). The bars are not visually emphasized with annotations, and within each year the multiple language bars are shown as adjacent (grouped) vertical bars rather than stacked.
